title: Read-only Claude shell check splits on `|`, `&&`, `||` without respecting quotes, so a quoted regex alternation (git grep -E "a|b") is refused as unbalanced quotes
outcome: Read-only Claude shell check splits on `|`, `&&`, `||` without respecting quotes, so a quoted regex alternation (git grep -E "a|b") is refused as unbalanced quotes
acceptance: A fail-first test shows the current read-only check refusing `git grep -n -E "mod tests|cfg\(test\)" -- <file>` (and `rg -e "a|b" <file>`) with the 'unbalanced quotes' refusal

The read-only command check (src/claude.rs:614-615) and its refusal explanation (src/claude_read_only_refusal.rs:171-172) split a line into segments only at unquoted `|`, `&&` and `||`, using one shared quote-aware splitter, so the decision and its explanation cannot disagree

Tests pin that a quoted `|`, `&&` or `||` inside single or double quotes stays inside its argument, that real unquoted pipes and chains are still split and vetted segment by segment, and that unbalanced quotes are still refused; no command that is refused today for a write or for unsupported syntax becomes allowed
